# Findings in one page

Short version of what the study shows, with the numbers that are in
`results/versions/table_final.csv`. Every figure and table in this repository is generated by
the scripts in `src/`; nothing is hand-edited.

## 1. Defect type dominates defect strength

Clean NEU-CLS reference: 99.63% test accuracy. Ten percentage points of label confusion cost
1.11 points; the mildest Gaussian noise costs 20.00 and the strongest 67.41. The four other
families sit in between (blur 12.96-22.96, salt-and-pepper 0.37-14.07, JPEG 0.37-12.96).

## 2. Families have different curve shapes

Gaussian noise is a cliff (sigma 8 -> 16 loses 35.93 points), blur is a gentle slope, and
salt-and-pepper / JPEG are threshold-like: nearly free until the last level, then a step down.

## 3. Stacked defects are not additive

Adding defect types one at a time gives 46.85 -> 60.00 -> 65.74 -> 78.33 -> 68.89. The
recovery happens because JPEG compression and motion blur are low-pass operations that remove
the high-frequency noise injected first; a second defect can *hide* the dominant one. Any
catalogue that records only "how dirty" a version is, not *which* defects it has, will
mis-rank its own data.

## 4. A fidelity-based quality score fails

Q1 = label consistency x class balance x sharpness, all training-free, monotone within every
family, but uncorrelated with accuracy across families (Spearman rho = -0.011, p = 0.96,
n = 26). Fidelity is not a common scale: JPEG artefacts destroy measured sharpness while
leaving the class-discriminative texture intact, and additive noise *raises* sharpness.

## 5. Reference-model agreement works, with a known boundary

RMA = fraction of training items whose delivered label matches a network trained on the clean
split. rho = 0.825 (p = 2.1e-7) over 26 versions; 0.822 over the 21 single-axis versions.
It fails on the cumulative series (rho = -0.60, n = 5) because it measures transfer from the
clean distribution, not the difficulty of the delivered task.

## 6. It is usable as a gate and as a repair guide

- Gate: RMA threshold 0.805 separates versions that lose more than 5 points from the rest with
  precision 1.00 and recall 0.94 (F1 0.97); the one miss is the mildest Gaussian noise.
- Repair: replacing the worst-scored 20% of the training files of the worst version
  (Gaussian sigma = 32, 32.22%) with clean originals recovers 99.63%; 50% adds nothing.

## 7. What does not transfer

- Backbone: ordering survives (Kendall tau = 0.87 on six versions), absolute numbers drop.
- Dataset: on KolektorSDD2 every corruption costs at most 2.29 points (against 67.41 here), so
  a cost table must be re-measured per dataset - which is exactly the argument for a cheap
  score.
